stories.headline: Lin Gaoyuan plans table tennis return for Guangdong at China's National Championships after drift racing season
stories.summary: Lin Gaoyuan, the former China international and world champion, plans to return to table tennis at the National Championships for Guangdong after a season of drift racing.
body: Lin Gaoyuan plans to return to competitive table tennis and play for Guangdong at China's National Championships, China News Service reported on Monday.

The former China international and world champion has spent much of the year in motorsport and drove in the annual final of the 2026 Royal Drift China Series. He said the new sport had given him a different kind of competitive experience.
The National Championships are China's domestic championships, contested by provincial teams. The dates of Lin's return have not been announced.

stories.headline: Women's Bundesliga: Weinheim beat Berlin Eastside 6-1 in front of 450 fans as Dachau win Bavarian derby
stories.summary: TTC Weinheim stayed top of the women's Bundesliga with a 6-1 win over the long-time champions TTC Berlin Eastside on Sunday, and TSV Dachau beat TuS Fürstenfeldbruck 6-2.
body: TTC Weinheim beat TTC Berlin Eastside 6-1 in the women's Bundesliga on Sunday, in a top-of-the-table match played in Wald-Michelbach in front of 450 spectators. Shi Qi won her doubles and her singles against a Berlin side that looked tired.
Weinheim have won all three of their matches, 18 individual matches to four, and lead SV DJK Kolbermoor on game difference. Berlin, who have dominated the league for years, have won two and lost two.
TSV Dachau beat TuS Fürstenfeldbruck 6-2 in the first Bavarian derby between the two clubs, with both teams missing their No 1. Dachau are third with two wins from three.
Berlin play at TTG Bingen/Münster-Sarmsheim on Saturday 14 November. Weinheim travel to Fürstenfeldbruck on 21 November and to Dachau the next day.

stories.headline: Pro A: Joué-lès-Tours come from 2-0 down at Quimper as Lys Lille Métropole win in Manosque
stories.summary: Joué-lès-Tours recovered from 2-0 down to beat Quimper 3-2 in the women's Pro A on Sunday, and Lys Lille Métropole, who started the day bottom, beat Alliance Nîmes/Montpellier 3-2 in the last game of the last match.
body: Joué-lès-Tours came from 2-0 down to win 3-2 at Quimper in the fourth round of the women's Pro A on Sunday. He Li, Taneesha Kotecha and Cléa De Stoppeleire won the last three matches, De Stoppeleire beating Audrey Zarif to settle the tie. Quimper had won 3-1 at Metz, the double defending champions, in the previous round.

Lys Lille Métropole, without a win before Sunday, beat Alliance Nîmes/Montpellier 3-2 in Manosque, the first women's Pro A match played in the town, in front of more than 200 spectators. Bruna Takahashi and Rachel Moret won matches for Nîmes/Montpellier, but Lille took the last two and the tie went to the fifth game of the fifth match. Hanna Haponova beat Wales's Anna Hursey 11-6 in a deciding game.

Saint-Denis won 3-1 at Poitiers, and Grand-Quevilly beat Saint-Quentin at home. Étival, unbeaten after three rounds, and the rest of the round's results are still to be published by the French federation.

stories.headline: Hacker claims to be selling data on 1.6 million people taken from the French Table Tennis Federation
stories.summary: A seller on a cybercriminal forum says it holds records on 1.6 million people from France's table tennis federation, which has not confirmed a new breach.
body: A hacker has offered for sale on a cybercriminal forum what it says are records on 1,645,606 people taken from the French Table Tennis Federation (FFTT), two French data-breach websites reported on Thursday. The federation has not publicly confirmed the claim.

The seller says the files include names, dates of birth, contact details and licence records, along with 1,864 identity documents and 383 proofs of address. A sample of 925 records examined by Fuites Infos and Cyberattaque.org held identity, contact and licence details, including those of minors, and for many players the date of their medical certificate and the name of the doctor who signed it. Neither site found passwords or bank details in the sample.

The number claimed is far higher than the FFTT's membership, which Cyberattaque.org puts at about 246,000 licensed players this season, and the newest records in the sample date from October 2025. Cyberattaque.org said the files could include historical records.

In September 2025 the FFTT said a compromised account had been used to take information in bulk from its database of licensed players, including names, dates and places of birth, nationality, addresses, email addresses and phone numbers. It said no bank or health data had been reached, that it had filed a complaint and informed France's data protection authority, the CNIL, and its cyber-security agency, ANSSI, and it urged members to be very careful with messages asking for passwords or bank details.

stories.headline: Youth Olympic Games: Lee Seungsoo wins South Korea's first table tennis medal since 2010
stories.summary: South Korea's Lee Seungsoo, 15, beat Hong Kong's Li Ki Ho 4-2 for the men's singles bronze in Dakar, taking the deciding game 15-13.
body: Lee Seungsoo won the Youth Olympic men's singles bronze in Dakar on Thursday, South Korea's first table tennis medal at the Games since the inaugural edition in Singapore in 2010.

The 15-year-old won the first three games against Hong Kong's Li Ki Ho, lost the fourth and then a 17-15 fifth, and took the sixth 15-13. In 2010 Kim Donghyun and Yang Haeun won mixed team silver and Yang won women's singles bronze; South Korea had not won a medal at the two Games since.

Lee won all his group matches, came through a seven-game match in the last 16, won his quarter-final 4-1, then lost 4-2 in the semi-final to Japan's Ryusei Kawakami, who went on to win the gold. OSEN reported that Lee had won three of their eight previous meetings on the junior circuit. Lee and Heo Yerim reached the mixed doubles quarter-finals, where they lost to Taiwan's Lin Chin-ting and Chen Min-hsin.

Lee, who won the under-19 boys' singles at WTT Youth Star Contender Gangneung this year, is due to play his first senior event at WTT Contender Istanbul from 10 to 15 November, Sports Kyunghyang reported.

stories.headline: Annett Kaufmann calls for tighter rules on social media platforms during WTT Champions Frankfurt
stories.summary: Germany's Annett Kaufmann, who has received death threats online, has called for internet platforms to be regulated more strictly.
body: Annett Kaufmann has called for tighter regulation of internet platforms, saying abuse of athletes online has become far too normal.

"Hate is not an opinion," the 20-year-old German said at WTT Champions Frankfurt, adding that reading comments about other players sometimes makes her afraid and that words have power. Kaufmann said in March that she had received death threats on social media.
Kaufmann, who beat Hong Kong's Doo Hoi Kem in the last 32 on Wednesday, plays Japan's Hina Hayata in the last 16 on Friday at about 2.20pm UK time.

stories.headline: Youth Olympic Games: Ryusei Kawakami and Chen Min-hsin win the singles titles in Dakar
stories.summary: Japan's Ryusei Kawakami beat Colombia's Emanuel Otálvaro and Taiwan's Chen Min-hsin beat Singapore's Loy Ming Ying, both 4-2, in the Youth Olympic singles finals.
body: Japan's Ryusei Kawakami and Taiwan's Chen Min-hsin won the Youth Olympic singles titles in Dakar on Thursday evening, both by four games to two.

Kawakami, the top seed, won the first three games against Colombia's Emanuel Otálvaro, who won the next two before Kawakami closed out the match 11-6. Kawakami, who won the mixed doubles gold with Miku Matsushima on Tuesday, now has two gold medals in Dakar. Otálvaro, 16, had knocked out China's Li Hechen in the quarter-finals.
Chen, 17 and the fifth seed, beat Singapore's 16-year-old Loy Ming Ying, the 10th seed, 4-2. Chen also won the mixed doubles bronze with Lin Chin-ting.

Loy's silver equals Singapore's best Youth Olympic table tennis result, Isabelle Li's runner-up finish at the first Games in Singapore in 2010. "I am happy to be able to fly the Singapore flag," she said, adding that she struggled to return Chen's serve towards the end.

stories.headline: Quadri Aruna plans to retire from international table tennis after the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics
stories.summary: Nigeria's Quadri Aruna, 38, intends to stop playing for his country after the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics but will carry on in club leagues.
body: Quadri Aruna intends to retire from international table tennis after the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics, though he plans to keep playing club table tennis.

"I want to stop playing at international level that's after the Los Angeles Olympics," the 38-year-old told Brila FM, adding that he would still play in leagues. He left some room to change his mind: "Sometimes we think we will stop but it is God that knows everything."
Aruna became the first African player to reach an Olympic singles quarter-final, at Rio 2016. He plays for Atlanta Blazers in Major League Table Tennis this season.

stories.headline: Pablo Ramirez Rioja and Max Radiven win medals for England at WTT Youth Contender Szombathely
stories.summary: Pablo Ramirez Rioja took under-15 boys' singles silver and Max Radiven under-19 mixed doubles bronze as England sent 16 juniors to WTT Youth Contender Szombathely in Hungary.
body: Pablo Ramirez Rioja won silver in the under-15 boys' singles at WTT Youth Contender Szombathely in Hungary, losing the final 11-9, 11-5, 11-9 to Jayden Cai of the US. He won several matches in deciding games on the way, including his semi-final against Ireland's Peadar Sheridan.

Max Radiven, 17, from Edgware, took bronze in the under-19 mixed doubles with Croatia's Lana Benko. They came from two games down to beat his England teammate Jake Davidson and Poland's Weronika Wszolek 8-11, 11-13, 11-6, 11-3, 11-8, won two more five-game matches, then lost 12-10, 11-9, 11-7 to Poland's Jan Mrugala and Aleksandra Nawrocka in the semi-final. In the under-19 boys' singles the eighth seed beat the top seed, India's Nikkhil Mannath, 7-11, 11-8, 11-7, 11-7, before losing in the last 16 to Hungary's Lenard Szabo.

Ella Pashley reached the last 16 of the under-19 girls' singles, where she lost 11-9, 11-9, 15-13 to Hungary's Judit Nagy, the seventh seed. England took 16 players from under-11 to under-19, and the coach Ben Barlow said four reached the quarter-finals or better, calling the week "a learning curve for some of the players".
Radiven represents England Schools at the European School Games in Poreč, Croatia, this week.

body: Honoka Hashimoto, the Japanese defender ranked 14th in the world, has signed a sponsorship contract with the animation studio MAPPA, starting this month. It is the first time MAPPA has backed an individual athlete.

The chopper beat a leading Chinese player in the women's team final at the World Championships in May, when Japan took silver, and helped them win the Asian team title in October. She is not in the draw at WTT Champions Frankfurt this week.

stories.headline: Fan Zhendong's future at Borussia Düsseldorf is open as no player has a contract beyond this season
stories.summary: Borussia Düsseldorf will open contract talks this month with none of their players or their coach signed beyond this season, the club's manager, Andreas Preuß, has said.
body: Preuß told the Tischtennis Bundesliga that talks on new contracts are due in November and that he wants to speak to Fan Zhendong, but does not expect quick decisions. He said the open squad planning gave him "a bit of a headache".

Fan, the Olympic champion, joined Düsseldorf from their rivals 1. FC Saarbrücken in the summer. The record German champions have won all six of their league matches and lead the TTBL with a perfect 12-0 points record.

Preuß said Fan's arrival had changed everything from ticketing and merchandise to social media. The club have added two international sponsors, and their matches are shown live in more than 300 cinemas in China.
Düsseldorf have several home matches in November and December, and the city stages a WTT Feeder event at the end of November.

stories.summary: Yorkshire and Nottinghamshire both won all three of their matches at Ashford to lead the County Championships veterans Premier Division after its first weekend.
body: The reigning champions Yorkshire beat the division's two new counties, Lancashire and Sussex, 8-2 each and then beat Essex 9-1. They lead on 12 points, two clear of Nottinghamshire.
Nottinghamshire, runners-up for the past two seasons, beat Hertfordshire and Kent 7-3 and Essex 10-0.
Hertfordshire and Middlesex are next on seven points with two wins each. Lancashire are fifth after beating Sussex, while Kent, Sussex and Essex lost all three of their matches.
The division finishes at Nottingham TTC on the first weekend of March.

stories.headline: Desmond Douglas joins Birmingham table tennis hub helping older black men stay active
stories.summary: Desmond Douglas, the 11-time English national champion, has visited the Over-50s Black Men Forum's table tennis health hub in Handsworth, where he grew up.
body: Douglas joined last week's session at Handsworth Wellbeing Centre, played with members and met people he had known growing up in the area. BBC Midlands filmed the session for a report on Midlands Today.

The Over-50s Black Men Forum (O5BM) uses weekly table tennis as a way into physical activity, friendship and conversations about health for men who may not use traditional health services. The Birmingham hub is part of a wider expansion of its community programme.

Douglas, who reached No 7 in the world and played for Great Britain at the 1988 Seoul Olympics, told BBC Midlands that getting out and playing sport helps older men set aside bad thoughts, adding: "Mentally you're in a happier place."

stories.headline: Ken Green, who umpired at the 1977 World Championships in Birmingham, dies aged 93
stories.summary: Ken Green, the international umpire who officiated at the 1977 World Championships in Birmingham, has died aged 93.
body: Green qualified as a national umpire in 1976 and as an ITTF international umpire in 1980. As well as the home world championships in 1977, he umpired at the 1981 edition in Novi Sad, then in Yugoslavia, and at the Commonwealth Championships in Cardiff in 1973 and Edinburgh in 1979.
Born in 1933, he played in the Warrington and Bolton leagues in the north-west before moving to Peterborough, where he died last month after a short illness.
A celebration of his life will be held at St Botolph's Church, Longthorpe, at 1.15pm on Thursday 26 November, followed by committal at Peterborough Crematorium.

sources.name: Table Tennis England: Obituary: International Umpire Ken Green

stories.headline: Tischtennis Bundesliga: Bad Homburg beat Werder Bremen 3-1 as Csaba Andras wins twice
stories.summary: TTC OE Bad Homburg beat Werder Bremen 3-1 at home on Monday night, with Csaba Andras winning both his singles, as the Tischtennis Bundesliga returned after a seven-week break.
body: Andras opened with an 11-4, 11-5, 11-6 win over Marcelo Aguirre, and Finn Luu came from a game down to beat Kirill Gerassimenko 3-1 for a 2-0 lead.
Irvin Bertrand kept Werder in the match by beating Ivan Ban 11-9, 11-2, 11-4, but Andras sealed the win by beating Gerassimenko 11-5, 11-9, 6-11, 11-4.
It is a third league win of the season for Bad Homburg, who now have three wins and three defeats. Werder had hoped to stay in the top four, which qualifies for the play-off finals.
